question: For real x,y >= 0, graph the feasible region 2x + 3y <= 11 and 4x + y <= 9. Label every corner with exact coordinates. Maximise Z = 5x + 4y, showing Z at every corner and marking the complete optimum set. Also mark A = (1,1), B = (3,0), C = (8/5,13/5) and classify feasibility. This is continuous optimisation, not an integer problem.

qualitativeClaims.expected: The two constraint lines intersect at C: 2(8/5)+3(13/5)=11 and 4(8/5)+13/5=9.
Maximum Z=92/5 at {(8/5,13/5)}. A linear objective reaches its maximum at a polygon corner, and this corner's value strictly exceeds the other three.
A=(1,1) is feasible; B=(3,0) is infeasible because 4(3)+0=12>9; C=(8/5,13/5) is feasible and lies on both constraint lines.
